rows.reason: The body publishes member maxima into each group's per-slot native detection record (+1E8h + slot*34h), unregisters its observer and dispatches effective-level changes. This host folds maxima into temporary Rec values inside group(), discards the member lists, and records publication without a native group detection/observer/delegate object. Passing its already-folded level through scratch storage would only round-trip the host answer; publishing real detection state requires broader recon storage changes.

The existing body traverses gun+3F0h -> owner+538h -> native platform pointer array+94h, indexed by gun+38Ch, then calls SetTargetAngles. GameGunRow retains a flattened rest pair/rest_authored flag, arcs and angles, but no native owner/platform-array hierarchy. A small retained-image view is unavailable; wiring would require manufacturing the missing object chain plus the broad Seg53Host adapter. No replacement body or synthetic hierarchy was added.

The body queries owner IsKindOf(2), owner vslot140 then vslot114 for a real director, allocates and retains a 14h bridge at ai+64h, and forces its initial Apply. attach_passes retains only independent countdown/cache/category fields; GunneryPassBinding::has_director_bridge always answers true. No native AI/owner/director identity or bridge allocation is retained. A scratch bridge with canned owner/director answers would not replace the host's live state.

The body owns a native sentinel list at F899C4, list size, critical-section owner/counter, 54h image HitRecord assignment and shot entity vslot5C(29h). The live host queue is std::deque<DeferredHit> with typed records, owned part vectors and replay side state. It has no native list/lock/record/shot images. A callback that merely push_back's the same DeferredHit would leave native list logic on unrelated scratch storage and fail the counting rule.
